    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401513/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In my current factory I use a very clean train setup: there is one very long main 2+2 line consisting of 2 rails per direction which connects all mining outposts with the main factory in a linear fashion. From this main line, secondary 1+1 lines branch off to close-by outposts.</p>
<p>All these branches are partial T-junctions, i.e., if the main line goes West-East, with the factory in the east, and the outpost is to the South, then trains can go West-&gt;East, East-&gt;West, East-&gt;South or South-&gt;East, but not South-&gt;West or West-&gt;South.</p>
<p>This is the simpler version I have, where the trains come from the East, go South to the outpost, then join the main line again towards the East:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/7o3M4.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/7o3M4.png"/></a></p>
<p>Often trains can also come from the East and cross to the South - but this case should be ignored for this question to keep it manageable. If you look closely, as regarding this questions, both designs are equivalent. I want to solve the problem of a West-&gt;East and a South-&gt;East train conflicting.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/HXRmy.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/HXRmy.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>So far so good, connecting everything with signals and chain signals so it's correctly signaled is easy. The problem occurs when a train wants to travel South-&gt;East and another train goes West-&gt;East. When the stars align just wrongly, either train stops to let the other pass and a <em>lot</em> of time is lost.</p>
<p>To battle this, I am placing regular lane switches along the main line - i.e. places where a train going West-&gt;East can switch between the two rails going in that direction. I've placed one switch before each of these junctions. A human driver coming along in the West-&gt;East direction would see the other train coming from the South, and quickly hop onto the North rail, leaving the junction open for the other train.</p>
<p>Unfortunately, in some tests I've done, it doesn't seem like the trains are "getting it", all the time; i.e. often the train speeding along West-&gt;East sticks to the South rail, forcing the other train to stop and wait (or vice versa); frustratingly, it could just as well switch to the North rail at little to no cost.</p>
<p>Is there a way to encourage this to happen more frequently?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401514/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As a general rule, trains don't change their routes “in real time” in response to what other trains are doing — they make a plan when they start moving and then update it only if they're actually blocked from continuing (or a few other cases). If you want your tracks to be used differently, you'll have to change their length or connectivity.</p>
<p>I'm not sure if this will actually be more efficient, but here is an idea to attempt to improve the behavior: Instead of treating your 2 tracks equivalently (any train can enter any track), make the outer (north) track “slow” and the inner (south) track “fast”.</p>
<ol>
<li>Remove the part of the junction that allows the train heading south→east to use the north track, so it always enters onto the south track.</li>
<li>Make the south track artificially slightly longer (add an unnecessary curve down and up in various places) so that trains prefer the north track if there's space on it.</li>
</ol>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In my current factory I use a very clean train setup: there is one very long main 2+2 line consisting of 2 rails per direction which connects all mining outposts with the main factory in a linear fashion. From this main line, secondary 1+1 lines branch off to close-by outposts.</p>
<p>All these branches are partial T-junctions, i.e., if the main line goes West-East, with the factory in the east, and the outpost is to the South, then trains can go West-&gt;East, East-&gt;West, East-&gt;South or South-&gt;East, but not South-&gt;West or West-&gt;South.</p>
<p>This is the simpler version I have, where the trains come from the East, go South to the outpost, then join the main line again towards the East:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/7o3M4.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/7o3M4.png"/></a></p>
<p>Often trains can also come from the East and cross to the South - but this case should be ignored for this question to keep it manageable. If you look closely, as regarding this questions, both designs are equivalent. I want to solve the problem of a West-&gt;East and a South-&gt;East train conflicting.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/HXRmy.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/HXRmy.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>So far so good, connecting everything with signals and chain signals so it's correctly signaled is easy. The problem occurs when a train wants to travel South-&gt;East and another train goes West-&gt;East. When the stars align just wrongly, either train stops to let the other pass and a <em>lot</em> of time is lost.</p>
<p>To battle this, I am placing regular lane switches along the main line - i.e. places where a train going West-&gt;East can switch between the two rails going in that direction. I've placed one switch before each of these junctions. A human driver coming along in the West-&gt;East direction would see the other train coming from the South, and quickly hop onto the North rail, leaving the junction open for the other train.</p>
<p>Unfortunately, in some tests I've done, it doesn't seem like the trains are "getting it", all the time; i.e. often the train speeding along West-&gt;East sticks to the South rail, forcing the other train to stop and wait (or vice versa); frustratingly, it could just as well switch to the North rail at little to no cost.</p>
<p>Is there a way to encourage this to happen more frequently?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401514/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As a general rule, trains don't change their routes “in real time” in response to what other trains are doing — they make a plan when they start moving and then update it only if they're actually blocked from continuing (or a few other cases). If you want your tracks to be used differently, you'll have to change their length or connectivity.</p>
<p>I'm not sure if this will actually be more efficient, but here is an idea to attempt to improve the behavior: Instead of treating your 2 tracks equivalently (any train can enter any track), make the outer (north) track “slow” and the inner (south) track “fast”.</p>
<ol>
<li>Remove the part of the junction that allows the train heading south→east to use the north track, so it always enters onto the south track.</li>
<li>Make the south track artificially slightly longer (add an unnecessary curve down and up in various places) so that trains prefer the north track if there's space on it.</li>
</ol>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm trying to build the Lakeview house and no matter what, the furniture bench doesn't want to appear in the main hall.</p>
<p>I'm not using a steward.</p>
<p>I'm able to decorate the entry way and the east and north and south wings and the basement, but simply no furniture in the main room where the fireplace and the table is supposed to be, also no furniture upstairs, no double bed, no kids beds, nothing, and no bench in the back room of main hall.</p>
<p>I have tried adding and removing benches from the bench outside with no luck.</p>
<p>I've even started a new game, because I don't want an unfinished house hanging around on my map, on the New save I still experience the same problem.</p>
<p>Is there any way to fix this?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm trying to build the Lakeview house and no matter what, the furniture bench doesn't want to appear in the main hall.</p>
<p>I'm not using a steward.</p>
<p>I'm able to decorate the entry way and the east and north and south wings and the basement, but simply no furniture in the main room where the fireplace and the table is supposed to be, also no furniture upstairs, no double bed, no kids beds, nothing, and no bench in the back room of main hall.</p>
<p>I have tried adding and removing benches from the bench outside with no luck.</p>
<p>I've even started a new game, because I don't want an unfinished house hanging around on my map, on the New save I still experience the same problem.</p>
<p>Is there any way to fix this?</p>
</div>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm trying to build the Lakeview house and no matter what, the furniture bench doesn't want to appear in the main hall.</p>
<p>I'm not using a steward.</p>
<p>I'm able to decorate the entry way and the east and north and south wings and the basement, but simply no furniture in the main room where the fireplace and the table is supposed to be, also no furniture upstairs, no double bed, no kids beds, nothing, and no bench in the back room of main hall.</p>
<p>I have tried adding and removing benches from the bench outside with no luck.</p>
<p>I've even started a new game, because I don't want an unfinished house hanging around on my map, on the New save I still experience the same problem.</p>
<p>Is there any way to fix this?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<h2>Setup:</h2>
<p>Summon the villager:</p>
<pre><code>/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}
</code></pre>
<p>Then I set up a scoreboard to keep track of his sleep:</p>
<pre><code>/scoreboard objectives add Josh dummy
</code></pre>
<h2>Commands:</h2>
<p>I will place this command in a stand-alone repeating command block:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] store result score @s Josh run data get entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value 1
</code></pre>
<p>This will grab his <code>last_slept</code> data, I don't actually know what it means but every time he jumps into the bed it is set to a number.</p>
<p>The next command in a repeating command block will then set the time right before dawn:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Josh matches 1.. run time set 23970t
</code></pre>
<p>You could also set it to <code>24000t</code> but then Josh would just jump out of bed right away.</p>
<p>This next command will be placed in a chain command block and reset his <code>last_slept</code> value:</p>
<pre><code>execute as @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] if score @s Josh matches 1.. run data modify entity @s Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<hr/>
<h2>Additional:</h2>
<p>If you wouldn't like to skip the night that fast you could set up a scoreboard that starts increasing when Josh gets in bed. Then set up commands that track the scoreboard in intervals so you could speed thru the night instead of just skipping it.</p>
<p>Something like this:</p>
<p><em>Repeating command block</em></p>
<pre><code>execute if score @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"}] Josh matches 1.. run scoreboard players add &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 1
</code></pre>
<p>You could use any player name or entity, like Josh himself, or set a fake player by just entering anything for the <code>&lt;Name&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>Then set up a few commands to add time in intervals:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches 100..100 run time add 1000t
</code></pre>
<p>This would add 1000 to the time when the score has reached 100. In a repeating command block that would be after 5 seconds. And then add however many you'd like depending on how fast/smooth you'd like it to be.</p>
<p>You would then also change the previous command in the chain command block to execute whenever the new <code>&lt;Score&gt;</code> have reached the highest number, which you would choose, so it would properly reset the data of Josh:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run data modify entity @e[nbt={CustomName:"{\"text\":\"Josh\"}"},limit=1] Brain.memories.minecraft:last_slept.value set value 0
</code></pre>
<p>Then you'd also need to reset your increasing score with a similar command, but make sure to do that after you set Josh's data to 0, otherwise it might increase a bit until Josh's data has been reset.</p>
<p>Could be placed in a chain command block after the last command:</p>
<pre><code>execute if score &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; matches num..num run scoreboard players set &lt;Name&gt; &lt;Score&gt; 0
</code></pre>
<p>And because Josh's data value got set to 0 the score won't start increasing until he goes to bed.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>
